# dsh-litnotes · The Margin Desk
> **Put the AI in the margin, not in another window.**
A local-first AI literature desk that plugs into the DeepSeek Harness Web UI: a paper library, bilin
gual reading, annotations and AI conversation that sit on the page, and a knowledge graph grown out
nnotations and AI conversation that sit on the page, and a knowledge graph grown out of your papers.
**English** · 简体中文
Every screenshot was captured from the plugin running for real; the sample paper is *Attention Is Al
l You Need*, parsed by the local engine with no upload.
## Why the margin
Most AI reading tools put the conversation in a floating window: ask a question, switch back to the
text, hunt for the quote — attention split in two. dsh-litnotes answers differently: **AI belongs in
the margin, just as annotations always have.**
- **Your eyes never leave the page.** The paper and the margin are two independent reading surfaces
— scrolling one never drags the other. Annotations and AI answers are pinned to their place in the t
ext, and a 1px tether ties each margin entry back to its sentence. Hover either end and the other li

ghts up.
- **Evidence before conclusions.** Every answer carries `[n]` citations: hover to preview t
he quoted sentence, click to jump back to it. Quotes are validated verbatim, then checked again for

whether they actually support the claim; unverified citations never become annotations.
- **Order is
position.** Margin entries are ordered by where they sit in the text. Read the margin top to bottom
, and you read the paper front to back.
## At a glance

| **Library** — parse status, progress, filters and full-text search
| **Import and parse** — drop,
pick a file or paste a link; three parse engines

| **Reading desk** — four aspect inks, margin notes, click a highlight for its annotation card
| **B
ilingual reading** — original and translation, paragraph by paragraph

| **Select to act** — highlight, annotate, ask AI, translate, copy
| **AI in the margin** — citation
s jump to the source, follow-ups, export

| **Per-paper knowledge graph** — the concepts, methods and findings inside one paper
| **Library gr
aph** — every paper aggregated into topics

| **AI 精读** — whole-paper close reading with a page-anchored report
| **Annotated by close reading**
— interpretive notes across the paper, not title/author metadata

| **Dark mode · reading**
| **Dark mode · graph**
## Features
### Reading

- Original, bilingual and translation-only modes; the text column uses the full paper width by
defau

lt, with adjustable scale, page marks and outline; formulas rendered locally with KaTeX,
figures and

tables kept in page order.
- Reading position, mode and panel widths are persisted locally — reopen

ing a paper returns to where you left off.
- The margin can show only your notes or only AI annotati
ons, and can be filtered by aspect.
### Annotations and the margin
- Four aspects — definition/background, method, result, limitation/context — each with its own ink.

Highlights, margin notes and AI annotations live in the same column.
- Click a highlight to open its

annotation card: the note, the quoted source, and **edit / delete** actions.
- After a re-parse, an
notations are re-anchored by their verbatim quote; ones that cannot be re-anchored are flagged as st
ale instead of being silently dropped.
### Grounded AI conversation
- Answers are generated only from the current paper's parsed text and streamed; stop, regenerate and

follow-up questions are supported.
- Citations are validated before they are shown; unverified cita
tions are dimmed and never become annotations. A citation in an answer jumps straight back to its se

ntence.
- Verified citations become AI annotations in their aspect color, carrying model and convers

ation provenance.
- Preset questions sit right above the composer in every scope, and the composer c

an be
answered by typing, by a preset, or by a follow-up.
- Questions default to the **whole paper**

(no paragraph is attached for you); the per-paragraph
**Ask AI about this paragraph** button next t

o translate/annotate narrows the focus to one
paragraph, and a text selection narrows it to the sele

ction — the composer chip always shows
which scope is active.
- Conversation history is stored per p
aper locally, can be cleared and exported as Markdown.
### Close reading (AI 精读)

- One action reads the **whole paper**, section by section, with a rolling reading memory — not a
sa

mpled head plus retrieval hits.
- It writes **many interpretive, evidence-anchored annotations** (24

by default, coverage-checked)
and explicitly rejects title/author/venue metadata and notes that mer

ely restate their quote.
- It produces a **structured close-reading report** — problem, gap, contrib

utions with evidence
strength, method, evaluation, findings, limitations, open questions, argument m

ap, glossary,
reading path and verdict — and every point jumps back to its page (`原文 p.N`).
- Transp

arent about what it read: sections read, annotations, coverage, model calls, duration and
tokens are

shown. The run is cancellable, cached and re-runnable; cancelling never loses the
previous report o

r annotations.
- Configurable through the `ai.deepRead*` keys (call cap, source cap, annotation cap,

per-call
output budget, synthesis digest, coverage pass, adjudication).
### Knowledge graphs
[该节后续省略]
## Data and privacy
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- Files, parse results, annotations, conversations and graphs stay on this machine. Only an explicit

cloud parse uploads the source file to MinerU.
- AI questions send only the bounded retrieved conte

xt (the relevant passages), never the whole library.
- The MinerU token lives in the DSH credential
store and is never returned to the browser or written to logs.
## Compatibility
- On-disk JSON uses stable version-1 envelopes and is compatible with the pre-refactor 0.3.0 format:

an existing library loads **without migration**.
- The plugin package has **zero runtime npm depend
encies**; the only external requests the client bundle makes are for the platform-provided React mod

ules.
- The source is strict TypeScript (`strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax
`, no `any`); the host and client halves speak one typed wire contract.
